newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air profits rise, distributes $97 million.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air profits rise, distributes $97 million.

text.p: Continental Airlines Tuesday reported a surprisingly big rise in fourth-quarter income as revenues improved, enabling the nation's fifth-largest airline to distribute $97 million to employees in 1996.

Profits rose to $47 million in the fourth quarter from $41 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share rose to 61 cents from 55 cents, beating analysts' consensus estimates of 53 cents, the company said.
Operating revenue grew to $1.56 billion from $1.42 billion.
Full-year 1996 earnings soared 42 percent to $319 million, or $4.11 per share, from $224 million, or $3.15 per share. Revenues rose to $6.36 billion from $5.83 billion.

The results include more than $68 million in profit-sharing payments (about 7 percent of annual wages) and at least $29 million in on-time bonuses ($590 per employee) for 1996 financial and operational performance.
"Continental is finally in solid financial health," said Larry Kellner, executive vice president and chief financial officer.

"In 1997 we will continue to do the same things that contributed to our success last year, as we continue to generate strong cash flow, pay off high interest debt and eliminate non-value added costs," he said.
In the fourth quarter, passenger revenue rose 10 percent to $1.4 billion, helping pre-tax income surge 82 percent from the 1995 period to $80 million, Continental said.
Revenue per available seat mile -- a measure of profitability -- rose to 9.42 cents from 9.38 cents in the 1995 fourth quarter, while Continental enlarged its seat capacity by over 8 percent.

Cost per available seat mile rose to 8.79 cents from 8.65 cents in the 1995 fourth quarter due to a 14 percent increase in jet fuel prices, the airline said. Higher wages and passenger-driven expenses were offset by productivity improvements.
At the end of the fourth quarter, Continental had a cash balance of more than $1 billion, by far the highest cash balance in the company's 62-year history.
Continental has more than 2,000 jet and Continental Express departures daily to 132 domestic and 58 international destinations.
Its class A stock fell 50 cents to $28.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
